Washington, D.C., October 26, 2026 – An Ipsos analysis of the October Reuters/Ipsos Core Political survey conducted October 22-26 finds that the Democratic Party holds a 9-point edge over the Republican Party among likely voters on the 2026 generic congressional ballot. Overall, 53% of likely voters say they would vote for or lean to the Democratic candidate in their district, compared with 44% who say they would vote for or lean to the Republican candidate. [...] As has been the case throughout the fall, Democrats continue to express more strong enthusiasm than Republicans toward voting in this fall's midterm elections.

Source: Survey of U.S. adults conducted Sept. 28-Oct. 4, 2026.

PEW RESEARCH CENTER

This analysis is among all registered voters – many of whom will not turn out in this November’s midterm elections. For example, 46% of those eligible voted in the 2022 midterm elections. [...] This is part of a larger report on the attitudes and dynamics shaping the 2026 midterm elections.

With several weeks to go until Election Day, Americans who are registered to vote favor Democrats over Republicans in the national race for the House of Representatives by an 8 percentage point margin (44% to 36%). About two-in-ten registered voters say they would vote for a third-party candidate or are not sure.
